Keywords: parallax, scrollytelling, story, scroll, layers, narrative, depth, chapters
Looks Like: A long page told in chapters, where background and foreground layers drift at different speeds as you scroll. Each chapter has one image, one idea and a short passage of text.
Use When: launch page, product story, campaign, annual report, museum, travel, brand history, event
Avoid When: Pages people scan for a phone number or price, and trust sectors such as law or medicine. Heavy motion hides the answer they came for.
Palette: Let one image or colour own each chapter and change it between chapters. Starting colours: #14213D page ink, #F4EFE6 paper chapter, #E07A1F one accent for the action, #2A6F6B second chapter tone.
Type Approach: A strong display face for chapter titles (Fraunces or Bricolage Grotesque) and a plain body face (Source Sans 3). Keep body at 18px with a 60-character line, and never put it over a moving layer.
Layout: Full-height chapters of 100svh with one text block each, offset from the centre. Leave a still band between chapters so readers can stop.
Motion: Layers move by transform only, at 0.2x to 0.6x of scroll speed; text reveals 400-600ms with ease-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion drop all offsets and show layers stacked and still.
Slop Habits: Parallax on every section instead of one chapter; layers that move text; a scroll-jacked page that blocks normal scrolling; stock landscape photos with no link to the business
Accessibility: Moving backgrounds can trigger vestibular symptoms, so honour prefers-reduced-motion (2.3.3) and give a Skip story link. Keep text contrast at 4.5:1 over every layer (1.4.3). Do not hijack scroll or hide content until it animates.
Performance: high: many large images and scroll-linked transforms; use compressed AVIF, lazy-load below the fold and only animate transform.
Checklist: Every chapter reads with layers still; reduced-motion shows no drift; text never sits on a moving layer; page scrolls at normal speed; tested on a mid-range phone

Aliases: International Typographic Style|Swiss Style|Grid-based design|Helvetica era
Keywords: swiss, grid, sans-serif, modular, objective, rational, flush-left, whitespace, typographic
Looks Like: Strict column grid, flush-left ragged-right text, one or two sans-serif faces and large type used as structure. Colour is flat and sparse, often one red or blue against white or black.
Use When: design studio, architecture, institution, conference, publisher, consultancy, portfolio, data report
Avoid When: Brands built on warmth, play or ornament, where such rigour reads as cold.
Palette: White or off-white ground, black type and one saturated signal colour. Starting colours: #FFFFFF ground, #111111 ink, #E30613 signal red, #767676 secondary text.
Type Approach: A neo-grotesque such as Archivo or Hanken Grotesk, in two weights only. Use a clear size ladder (14, 18, 28, 56, 112px), flush-left, with consistent leading on a baseline unit.
Layout: A 12-column grid with fixed gutters and a 8px baseline. Align every block to a column edge, leave whole columns empty and let rules and numbers organise content.
Motion: Almost none: 150-200ms colour change on hover, ease-out. Page transitions are cuts. Reduced motion needs no change beyond removing the hover transitions.
Slop Habits: Using Helvetica-like type with no grid beneath it; red accent on every element; centring everything; thin grey text everywhere for a minimal look
Accessibility: Grey secondary text often fails 4.5:1 (1.4.3), so test it. Keep a visible focus ring on links (2.4.7) and do not rely on red alone to mark state. Large type helps low-vision readers; keep it reflowing at 400% zoom (1.4.10).
Performance: low: flat colour, text and few images.
Checklist: Everything snaps to the grid; at most one accent colour; text measure 45-75 characters; secondary text passes 4.5:1; layout holds at 375px

Aliases: Heads-up display|Fantasy user interface|Cockpit UI|Sci-fi interface
Keywords: hud, sci-fi, fui, cockpit, telemetry, overlay, scanlines, monospace, readout, game
Looks Like: Thin lines, corner brackets, small numeric readouts and panels that float over a dark scene. Looks like instruments in a film cockpit.
Use When: game, esports, space, drone, hardware launch, film tie-in, data tool, developer product
Avoid When: Health, finance and public services, and anyone who needs to read long text. Fine glowing lines tire the eye.
Palette: Dark base with one or two bright line colours. Starting colours: #05080F base, #19E3FF line cyan, #FFB000 warning amber, #9FB3C8 label text.
Type Approach: A technical sans or mono for numbers and labels only (Share Tech Mono or Rajdhani) and a readable sans (IBM Plex Sans) for sentences. Set labels at 12-13px with 0.08em tracking, never body copy.
Layout: Panels in a modular grid with 1px borders, cut corners and tight 12-16px gaps. Dense in the centre, empty at the edges.
Motion: Panels draw in with a 300-500ms clip-path wipe, readouts tick at 1s with steps(). Under prefers-reduced-motion show the final state and stop tickers.
Slop Habits: Fake numbers that mean nothing; scanlines and flicker on every element; neon glow on all text; unreadable 9px labels
Accessibility: Thin cyan on dark can fail 3:1 for lines (1.4.11) and 4.5:1 for text (1.4.3). Flicker and flashing must stay under three per second (2.3.1). Pause any ticker (2.2.2). Decorative readouts get aria-hidden.
Performance: medium: many animated elements and possibly canvas; limit running animations and pause off-screen.
Checklist: Every number is true or marked as sample; no flashing over 3 per second; body text is a plain sans; line colours pass 3:1; ticker can be paused

Keywords: pixel, 8-bit, retro, game, sprite, bitmap, arcade, crisp, nostalgia
Looks Like: Chunky square pixels, limited palettes and hard-edged sprites with no smoothing. Borders and buttons look like stepped game windows.
Use When: indie game, game jam, arcade, retro shop, gaming cafe, community, kids event, music chiptune
Avoid When: Serious services and long reading, where a pixel font tires people. Not for brands with no link to games.
Palette: Limit to 4-8 flat colours with no gradients. Starting colours: #1B1B2F dark ground, #F5F0E1 light, #E43F5A accent red, #3DDC97 success green.
Type Approach: A pixel face for headings only (Press Start 2P or Pixelify Sans) at multiples of its design size, and a plain sans for paragraphs. Never scale pixel type to odd sizes.
Layout: Snap everything to an 8px grid; use stepped borders and generous space around text. Sprites sit in clear frames.
Motion: Frame-based sprites with steps() easing at 100-200ms per frame; no smooth tweens. Reduced motion shows a single static frame.
Slop Habits: Pixel font for all body text; blurry upscaled sprites; fake CRT scanlines over everything; coins and hearts as decoration with no meaning
Accessibility: Pixel fonts are slow to read, so keep body text in a plain face (1.4.3, 1.4.12). Use image-rendering: pixelated and give sprites alt text (1.1.1) or an empty alt if decorative. Focus rings must be chunky and visible (2.4.7).
Performance: low: small sprite sheets and flat colour.
Checklist: Sprites crisp at every size; body text in a plain face; palette under 8 colours; animation stops under reduced motion; alt text on meaningful sprites

Keywords: spatial, visionos, glass, depth, translucent, blur, floating, vibrancy, headset, panels
Looks Like: Rounded translucent glass panels that float above a soft background, with light edges and gentle shadows. Content has clear depth layers and large, calm targets.
Use When: vision app, spatial product, device launch, media app, presentation tool, 3D tool
Avoid When: Low-power devices and busy photo backgrounds that make glass text unreadable. Also anyone who needs high contrast.
Palette: Neutral translucent surfaces over a soft scene with one tint. Starting colours: #1C1C1E base, #F2F2F7 text, #0A84FF action blue, #3A3A3C panel edge.
Type Approach: A clear humanist sans (Figtree or DM Sans) in medium and semibold weights, 17px minimum, with generous leading. Follow Apple's HIG advice to keep text large and high contrast on glass.
Layout: Few large panels with 24-32px radius, 20-40px padding and wide spacing between targets. Group by depth: back, middle, front.
Motion: Hover lifts by 4-8px with 200-300ms ease-out; panels scale 1 to 1.02. Under prefers-reduced-motion use opacity change only, no scale or parallax.
Slop Habits: Blur on every card; glass over any photo regardless of contrast; stacked translucent panels nobody can read; shadows on everything
Accessibility: Blur backgrounds vary, so text on glass must be tested at 4.5:1 (1.4.3) against light and dark scenes, and add a solid fallback when prefers-reduced-transparency is set. Keep targets 44px or more (2.5.8) and focus rings visible (2.4.7).
Performance: medium: backdrop-filter is costly on large or stacked areas; limit to a few panels.
Checklist: Text passes 4.5:1 on glass over light and dark scenes; solid fallback exists; targets are 44px or larger; no more than three glass layers; reduced motion removes lift

Keywords: e-ink, paper, reader, grayscale, print, high-contrast, low-refresh, text, minimal
Looks Like: Black text on a grey-white page, with no gradients, no shadows and almost no animation. It looks like a book or an e-reader screen.
Use When: reading app, long articles, journal, documentation, library, newsletter, bookshop, notes
Avoid When: Brands that depend on colour photography or product shots. Colour accents are missing, so it may feel flat.
Palette: Greyscale with at most one dark accent. Starting colours: #F1EFE9 paper, #1A1A1A ink, #6B6B6B secondary text, #8A1C1C a single dark red for links.
Type Approach: A text serif for reading (Literata or Source Serif 4) at 19-21px, line height 1.6, 65-character measure. Headings in the same family at bolder weight.
Layout: A single centred column, wide margins, little chrome. Use thin rules sparingly and give images captions.
Motion: No animation; changes are instant. Page turns are plain links. Reduced motion needs no extra work.
Slop Habits: Fake paper texture images; sepia tint used as decoration; ghost buttons with thin grey outlines; tiny grey metadata everywhere
Accessibility: Light greys on paper often fail 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Let users resize text and reflow at 400% (1.4.10). Underline links so colour is not the only cue. Keep focus rings dark and thick (2.4.7).
Performance: low: text with almost no images or script.
Checklist: Body text passes 7:1 where possible; links are underlined; page works with no script; column holds at 375px; images have captions and alt text

Keywords: maximalist, chaos, collage, loud, stickers, clashing, zine, bold, overlap, youth
Looks Like: Overlapping type, stickers, clashing colour and mixed fonts packed into every corner. It looks like a bedroom wall or a zine, not a template.
Use When: streetwear, music, festival, youth brand, indie shop, fanzine, club night, creative collective
Avoid When: Banks, clinics, government and anything with a task to finish. Clutter slows people down.
Palette: Several loud colours used on purpose, with one calm area for reading. Starting colours: #FF3EA5 hot pink, #FFE500 yellow, #2B2BFF blue, #111111 ink, #FFFFFF reading panel.
Type Approach: Mix two or three distinct display faces (Rubik Mono One, Bagel Fat One) and keep a plain face (Work Sans) for text. Rotate headlines a few degrees, but keep paragraphs level.
Layout: Dense overlapping layers on a loose grid, with sticker-like images. Put a flat, wide reading panel behind the body text.
Motion: Stickers wobble or peel on hover, 200-400ms with a springy cubic-bezier. One looping movement at most. Reduced motion freezes all of it.
Slop Habits: Random emoji and stickers with no meaning; every element rotated; neon on neon text; a marquee strip on every page
Accessibility: Clashing colour often fails text contrast (1.4.3), so keep text on a flat panel. Loops must pause or stop (2.2.2) and nothing flashes over three per second (2.3.1). Keep tab order sensible when layers overlap.
Performance: medium: many layered images and effects; compress images and cap running animations.
Checklist: Text sits on a flat reading panel; every sticker relates to the brand; nothing flashes; loops can be paused; tab order follows the visible order

Keywords: organic, biomimetic, curves, natural, blob-free, soft, cellular, growth, fluid, shapes
Looks Like: Curved containers, uneven edges and shapes taken from leaves, cells or shells. Layouts bend around content instead of boxing it.
Use When: wellness, biotech, sustainable brand, garden, skincare, science museum, food producer, architecture
Avoid When: Data-heavy tools and anything needing fast scanning. Irregular shapes make rows hard to compare.
Palette: Earth and water tones with one lively accent. Starting colours: #EDF1E6 pale moss, #2F4A3A deep leaf, #C9602B clay accent, #7FA3A0 water.
Type Approach: A soft serif or humanist sans (Newsreader with Nunito Sans). Use generous size and slight weight contrast; avoid decorative script.
Layout: Asymmetric columns with clip-path or border-radius shapes, 48-96px section spacing. Keep text blocks rectangular inside curved frames.
Motion: Shapes breathe with 4-8s slow morphs of border-radius, ease-in-out. Reduced motion holds the first shape.
Slop Habits: Soft gradient blobs behind the hero; rounded corners on everything; leaf icons with no link to the product; the same wavy divider between every section
Accessibility: Text over curved image edges can lose contrast (1.4.3). Keep shapes decorative with aria-hidden. Slow morphing must be stoppable (2.2.2). Keep reading order the same as the visual order.
Performance: medium: clip-paths and SVG shapes cost little, but morphing large areas repaints.
Checklist: Shapes carry meaning from the brand; text stays on rectangular blocks; morph can be stopped; contrast checked on image edges; layout holds at 375px

Keywords: raw, brutalist, anti-design, unpolished, monospace, plain-html, hard-edge, rough, honest
Looks Like: Plain borders, system-looking type, visible structure and almost no decoration. It looks deliberately unfinished but is carefully built.
Use When: artist, zine, indie studio, collective, activism, experimental publisher, small press, portfolio
Avoid When: Trust sectors and nervous buyers, who read roughness as carelessness. Also brands whose clients expect polish.
Palette: Flat colours picked on purpose, with strong contrast. Starting colours: #FFFFFF page, #000000 ink, #0000EE link blue, #FFDD00 highlight.
Type Approach: Use a plain face in a stark way (Space Grotesk or Courier Prime for data) with underlined links and visible default sizes. Keep two sizes only: large and normal.
Layout: Single column or simple table-like layout, thick 2px borders, no rounded corners, and uneven but intentional whitespace.
Motion: Nothing moves except link state change. Cuts are instant. Reduced motion needs no extra work.
Slop Habits: Messy layout that is simply careless; ugly for its own sake with no concept; monospace for all body text; broken links and missing alt text excused as style
Accessibility: Rough does not excuse missing basics: keep contrast (1.4.3), visible focus (2.4.7), alt text (1.1.1) and proper headings. Default blue links on white pass; check any tint. Keep targets 24px or more (2.5.8).
Performance: low: little CSS, few images, no heavy script.
Checklist: The roughness has a reason you can state; all links and focus states work; alt text present; contrast passes; page still reads in plain HTML

Keywords: tactile, deformable, squish, soft, physical, press, spring, haptic, 3d, toy
Looks Like: Buttons and cards that look pressed from soft material and dent, stretch or bounce when touched. Light and shadow suggest thickness.
Use When: kids app, toy brand, game, creative tool, music app, playful product, onboarding, mobile app
Avoid When: Dense work tools and forms, where bouncing slows people. Also low-end phones.
Palette: Mid-tone surfaces with soft highlights and shadows. Starting colours: #E8E4F0 soft base, #5B4BDB press accent, #FFFFFF highlight, #B9B3CC shadow tone.
Type Approach: A rounded, friendly sans (Baloo 2 or Nunito) with chunky weights for labels; plain 16-18px for body. Do not use thin weights on soft surfaces.
Layout: Large rounded controls with 56px minimum height and clear gaps. Sparse screens: one action per view.
Motion: Press scales to 0.96 over 100ms, release springs back in 300-400ms with overshoot. Under prefers-reduced-motion use a colour change only.
Slop Habits: Soft shadows and inner glows on every element; bouncing on every scroll; low-contrast pastel labels; squircle everything
Accessibility: Soft light-on-light surfaces often fail 3:1 for control edges (1.4.11), so add an outline or stronger shade. Make press state visible without motion (2.4.7). Targets 44px or more (2.5.8). Respect reduced motion (2.3.3).
Performance: medium: layered shadows and spring animation; keep to transform and few shadows.
Checklist: Control edges pass 3:1; press state works without motion; targets are 44px or larger; reduced motion removes bounce; tested on a low-end phone

Aliases: Earthy minimal|Natural palette|Botanical calm|Warm earth tones
Keywords: nature, earthy, botanical, muted, handmade, grounded, organic, textures, warm, simple
Looks Like: Muted earth colours, simple photography of plants, soil and water, and plain layouts with a little texture. It looks grown, not decorated.
Use When: farm shop, florist, eco brand, outdoor gear, retreat, ceramics, herbal, garden centre
Avoid When: Tech products and anything urgent. The slow, soft tone can feel vague without clear actions.
Palette: Two earth tones and one deep neutral. Starting colours: #4B5B3A moss, #A5673F clay, #2B2A26 soil text, #D9CFB8 sand panel.
Type Approach: One serif with warmth for headings (Lora or Young Serif) and a clear sans for text (Mulish). Sizes steady, weights modest.
Layout: Spacious two-column sections that alternate image and text, with a few full-width photographs. Keep generous 80-120px section gaps.
Motion: Slow 400-600ms fades on image load and soft hover shifts, ease-out. Reduced motion shows everything at once.
Slop Habits: Cream background with terracotta accent by default; leaf icons in circles; stock flat-lay photos; the word sustainable with no proof
Accessibility: Muted greens and clay often drop below 4.5:1 for text (1.4.3), so darken them. Give photos useful alt text (1.1.1). Keep tap targets 44px or more (2.5.8).
Performance: low: mostly text and optimised photos.
Checklist: Photos are the owner's own; accent text passes 4.5:1; claims such as organic are backed up; spacing is consistent; layout holds at 375px

Keywords: cursor, pointer, hover, follow, magnetic, trail, interactive, desktop, playful
Looks Like: The pointer changes shape, follows elements or reveals content as it moves. Hover states carry much of the personality of the page.
Use When: portfolio, agency, creative studio, event, fashion, gallery, product showcase
Avoid When: Touch devices, which have no hover, and tasks needing speed. Also keyboard and screen reader users unless built carefully.
Palette: Neutral base with one contrast colour for the cursor. Starting colours: #0E0E10 base, #F5F5F0 light, #FF4D2E cursor accent, #8C8C94 muted.
Type Approach: A confident grotesque (Syne or Space Grotesk) for headlines, large enough to make hover targets. Body stays plain at 17-18px.
Layout: Large, widely spaced targets such as project names or images so the cursor effect has room. Keep the layout complete without hover.
Motion: Cursor follows with a 100-200ms lag using transform; hover scales by 1.1-1.3 over 200ms ease-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion use the normal pointer and no follow.
Slop Habits: A trailing blob cursor on every site; hiding the normal pointer with no fallback; magnetic buttons everywhere; hover-only content that touch users never see
Accessibility: Never hide the native cursor on controls without a visible replacement. Hover content must also work on focus and tap (1.4.13). Keep focus rings (2.4.7). Gate effects behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Performance: low: one small element updated by transform; throttle with requestAnimationFrame.
Checklist: Page works fully without a mouse; every hover reveal also shows on focus; effect is off on touch; native cursor still shows on text fields; reduced motion respected

Keywords: voice, speech, conversational, multimodal, assistant, audio, captions, hands-free, listening
Looks Like: A screen built around spoken input and replies, with large status text, captions and a few big buttons as backup. Little is visible at once.
Use When: smart display, car app, kitchen app, assistant, accessibility tool, support line, hands-free tool
Avoid When: Noisy or private places such as open offices, and complex data entry. Speech is slow for long lists.
Palette: Calm base with clear state colours for listening, thinking and error. Starting colours: #101820 base, #F2F5F7 text, #3DA5FF listening blue, #FFB84D attention amber.
Type Approach: A very legible sans (Atkinson Hyperlegible or Lexend) at 24px or larger for prompts and transcripts. One line of reply at a time.
Layout: One central prompt, a visible transcript and two or three large buttons at the bottom. Stack vertically with 24px gaps.
Motion: Status indicator pulses at 1.2s ease-in-out while listening; transcript lines appear in 200ms. Reduced motion shows a static label such as Listening.
Slop Habits: A pulsing orb as the only feedback; a chatbot with no typed alternative; synthetic reassurance such as I am here to help; hiding commands users need
Accessibility: Offer text and touch for everything spoken. Show captions for audio (1.2.1) and show state in words, not colour alone. Let users stop or slow audio (1.4.2). Targets 44px or more (2.5.8).
Performance: medium: audio streaming and recognition cost data and power; keep the interface itself light.
Checklist: Every spoken action has a typed or tap equivalent; replies show as text; state is written out; transcript is readable at 24px; errors say what to do next

Keywords: 3d, product, viewer, rotate, configurator, webgl, model, spin, showcase
Looks Like: A product shown as an object you can turn, zoom and recolour, on a plain stage with spare surroundings. The model is the centre of the page.
Use When: product launch, furniture, trainers, hardware, jewellery, car, gadget, configurator
Avoid When: Products with no meaningful shape, slow connections and people who need a quick price. A heavy viewer delays buying.
Palette: Neutral stage so the product colour leads. Starting colours: #F3F3F1 stage, #1B1B1B ink, #2A5BD7 action blue, #C7C7C2 floor shadow.
Type Approach: A clean sans (Manrope or Sora) for specs and labels, with large numerals for price. Keep labels short and near the hotspots.
Layout: Viewer takes 60 percent of the screen with controls and options beside or below it. Spec and price stay visible without scrolling on desktop.
Motion: Auto-rotate 12-20s per turn until touched; option changes ease 300-500ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop auto-rotate and show still angles.
Slop Habits: Slowly spinning model with no controls; glow behind the product; loading spinner longer than the page content; specs hidden inside the viewer
Accessibility: Provide plain photos and text specs (1.1.1). Make rotate, zoom and option controls keyboard operable with visible focus (2.1.1, 2.4.7). Auto-rotation must stop on request (2.2.2). Do not trap scroll inside the canvas.
Performance: high: model files and WebGL; compress with Draco, show a poster image first and load the viewer on interaction.
Checklist: A still photo loads first; keyboard can rotate and choose options; auto-rotate stops; page scrolls past the canvas; model under 5 MB where possible

Keywords: gradient, mesh, aurora, colour-field, blur, soft, background, wash, abstract
Looks Like: Soft overlapping colour fields that blend into one another, used as a background or as one large panel. Rarely it works as an image replacement.
Use When: music release, creative tool, event poster, album page, fashion launch, one-off campaign
Avoid When: Most business sites, where it is the default look of generated pages. Also trust sectors and anything with no story behind the colours.
Palette: Use two or three related colours with a strong neutral for text. Starting colours: #0F1020 ink, #F7F5FF text panel, #FF6B6B coral field, #FFC857 warm field, #2EC4B6 teal field.
Type Approach: A strong display face (Bricolage Grotesque or Syne) over the colour, with body text on a solid panel instead of the gradient. Large headings and short lines.
Layout: One bounded panel such as a poster or header band, not the whole page. Leave the rest solid so the colours mean something.
Motion: Colour fields drift over 20-40s with ease-in-out, or stay still. Under prefers-reduced-motion keep the static gradient.
Slop Habits: Aurora blob behind the hero of every page; purple and blue as the default; glassy cards on top; blurred glow behind a headline
Accessibility: Text on shifting colour changes contrast as it moves, so put it on a solid area (1.4.3). Avoid fast colour cycling (2.3.1). Make sure decoration has no meaning that only colour carries.
Performance: medium: large blurred layers repaint costly; use a pre-rendered image or small canvas and avoid animating blur.
Checklist: Gradient limited to one panel; text sits on a solid area; the colours come from the brand or product; no animation under reduced motion; reason for using it is written down

Keywords: editorial, magazine, grid, serif, headline, pull-quote, caption, photo-led, columns
Looks Like: Large serif headlines, columns of text, captions and a mix of image sizes laid out like a printed feature. Hierarchy comes from size and position.
Use When: publisher, magazine, journalist, agency, culture, restaurant guide, long read, newsletter
Avoid When: Transaction-heavy sites, where users need forms and prices before stories. Also very small screens with many columns.
Palette: Black and white with one editorial colour. Starting colours: #FAFAF7 paper, #151515 ink, #B3261E accent red, #5A5A55 caption text.
Type Approach: A high-contrast serif for headlines (Playfair Display or DM Serif Display) with a text serif or sans (Source Serif 4) for body. Set drop caps and captions in the body face at small size.
Layout: A 12-column grid collapsing to one on phones. Mix a lead story at wide span, smaller items beside and consistent gutters of 24px.
Motion: Light: 200-300ms link underline changes and one load reveal. Reduced motion removes the reveal.
Slop Habits: Italic word in every headline; uppercase eyebrow above each headline; drop caps with no reason; identical card grid for every story
Accessibility: Check caption and grey text contrast (1.4.3). Keep reading order the same as the visual order across columns. Give each photograph alt text or a caption that serves (1.1.1). Ensure columns reflow at 400% zoom (1.4.10).
Performance: low: text and a few images; set image sizes to avoid layout shift.
Checklist: Hierarchy is clear at a glance; reading order matches visual order; captions have contrast; each story has its own image; layout is one column at 375px

Aliases: RGB split|Glitch colour fringe|Channel shift|Chromatic fringe
Keywords: chromatic, aberration, rgb, split, glitch, fringe, offset, lens, distortion, colour-shift
Looks Like: Text or images with red and blue edges offset by a pixel or two, as if a lens or screen were slightly misaligned. Best as an accent on one element.
Use When: music, club night, game, tech event, film poster, music video, experimental art
Avoid When: Anything people must read at length, as the fringe tires the eye. It also fails for dyslexic readers when used on body text.
Palette: Dark base with the split in red, green and blue light. Starting colours: #0B0B0F base, #FF2A4D red channel, #2AD8FF blue channel, #F2F2F2 text.
Type Approach: A bold heavy face for the split headline only (Anton or Bebas Neue); body in a plain sans (Public Sans). Never split small text.
Layout: One hero line or image with the effect and plenty of plain space around it. Use it once per page.
Motion: A 2-4px offset that flickers for 150-300ms on hover or load; static otherwise. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the offset still or turn it off.
Slop Habits: RGB split on every heading; constant glitch jitter; offset on body text; combining with scanlines and noise as a default look
Accessibility: Flashing and jitter can trigger seizures, so stay well under three flashes per second (2.3.1). Split text can drop under 4.5:1 (1.4.3); keep an unsplit copy for reading. Hide the duplicate layers from screen readers with aria-hidden.
Performance: low: pure CSS text-shadow; heavy image filters cost more.
Checklist: Effect is used once; body text is unsplit; nothing flashes over 3 per second; reduced motion removes flicker; headline still readable when effect is off

Aliases: Retro film|Analogue photo|Film grain|Polaroid style|Vintage print
Keywords: vintage, analogue, film, grain, polaroid, retro, warm, faded, photo, print
Looks Like: Warm faded colour, soft grain, white photo borders and typewriter or old print type. It looks like a pinned-up developed roll.
Use When: photographer, wedding, cafe, vinyl shop, vintage store, travel journal, band, boutique hotel
Avoid When: Tech, finance and any site wanting a sharp modern look. Heavy filters can also hide product detail.
Palette: Faded warm tones with a dark brown ink. Starting colours: #F1E6D0 aged paper, #3B2A20 ink, #C8553D faded red, #6F8F72 dusty green.
Type Approach: A period serif or slab for headlines (Libre Baskerville or Zilla Slab) and a plain serif or sans for text. Typewriter faces (Special Elite) only for captions and dates.
Layout: Photographs with white borders and slight rotation of 1-2 degrees in a loose grid, with handwritten-style captions. Keep text on flat blocks.
Motion: Photos settle into place with 300-500ms ease-out; grain stays static. Reduced motion shows photos straight with no movement.
Slop Habits: Heavy sepia on everything; fake scratches and dust overlays; cream background with terracotta accent by default; typewriter font for body copy
Accessibility: Faded text and busy grain hurt readability; keep body 7:1 on flat paper (1.4.3). Do not put text over grain textures. Give photographs alt text (1.1.1). Static grain is fine; animated grain should stop.
Performance: medium: grain overlays and large photos; use a small tiled noise image and compress photos.
Checklist: Text is on flat paper, not grain; photographs are the owner's own; filters leave detail visible; alt text present; grain does not animate

Keywords: bauhaus, geometric, primary-colours, circle, triangle, square, modernist, functional, 1920s, poster
Looks Like: Circles, squares and triangles in red, yellow and blue with heavy black type and bold diagonals. Layouts are flat and functional, like a 1920s poster.
Use When: design school, exhibition, architecture, furniture, culture event, publisher, museum, education
Avoid When: Soft or luxury brands, and heavy text sites. The loud geometry competes with long reading.
Palette: Primary colours with black and an off-white ground. Starting colours: #F2EBDD ground, #111111 ink, #D7261E red, #F5C400 yellow, #1F4E9C blue.
Type Approach: A geometric sans (Jost, based on Futura, or Josefin Sans) in bold for headings, set lowercase or sentence case, with plain body text. Use rotated type once at most.
Layout: An asymmetric grid with large shapes placed on diagonals, strong rules and a clear hierarchy. Keep text blocks flat and aligned to the grid.
Motion: Shapes slide or rotate once on load, 400-600ms ease-in-out; hover swaps colour in 150ms. Reduced motion shows the final positions.
Slop Habits: Random circles, squares and triangles as wallpaper; primary colours at equal weight everywhere; Futura-like font with no grid; red-black-white copied from a poster with no link to the brand
Accessibility: Yellow on white fails 4.5:1 (1.4.3); use black text on yellow. Do not carry meaning by colour alone. Rotated type must stay readable and keep DOM order (1.3.2). Visible focus rings (2.4.7).
Performance: low: flat shapes in CSS or SVG.
Checklist: Shapes follow a grid, not scatter; each primary colour has a job; text on yellow is black; reading order matches the DOM; layout holds at 375px

Aliases: Black and white|Monochrome minimal|Mono palette|Greyscale design
Keywords: monochrome, minimal, black-white, greyscale, stark, typography, contrast, whitespace, simple
Looks Like: Black, white and a few greys, with type, space and photography doing all the work. No accent colour competes for attention.
Use When: architect, photographer, studio, portfolio, fashion, consultancy, product page, gallery
Avoid When: Brands that depend on colour to be recognised, and interfaces needing colour status such as errors.
Palette: Pure neutrals with maybe one tone of grey for lines. Starting colours: #FFFFFF page, #0A0A0A ink, #6E6E6E secondary text, #E5E5E5 rule.
Type Approach: One strong family in two weights (Familjen Grotesk or Schibsted Grotesk) at a big scale ladder; contrast comes from size, not colour.
Layout: Wide margins, large type, a few well-cut images and a lot of empty space. Align to a simple 12-column grid.
Motion: Minimal: 200ms opacity or underline on hover, ease-out. One gentle load reveal at most. Reduced motion removes it.
Slop Habits: Thin light grey type that fails contrast; identical black buttons everywhere; a grey card around every block; empty space with no content planned for it
Accessibility: Without colour, make state clear with text, weight and underline (1.4.1). Mid greys often fail 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Keep strong focus rings in black or white (2.4.7, 2.4.11).
Performance: low: little CSS, few images.
Checklist: Secondary text passes 4.5:1; state is shown without colour; photography is strong enough to carry the page; focus ring is visible; spacing is consistent

Keywords: luxury, restrained, hotel, jeweller, tailor, architect, fine-type, space, muted, bespoke
Looks Like: Very few colours, wide margins, fine serif type and large, still photographs. Nothing shouts and there are no sale banners.
Use When: boutique hotel, jeweller, tailor, architect, interior designer, estate agent, private dining, atelier
Avoid When: Discount sellers and busy marketplaces, and anyone who needs to sell on price. The calm tone makes offers look cheap.
Palette: Two neutrals and one deep tone, with no bright accent. Starting colours: #F4F1EC stone, #1E1C1A ink, #8B7355 bronze, #5E6B63 sage-grey.
Type Approach: A refined serif for headings (Cormorant Garamond or Cormorant) in light weight at large size and a light sans for text (Jost or Hanken Grotesk). Add 0.02em spacing at small sizes only.
Layout: Generous 120-160px section space, one image per screen and short text blocks on a narrow column. Keep navigation to five items.
Motion: Slow 600-900ms fades and gentle image scale on hover, cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). Reduced motion removes the scale and fades.
Slop Habits: Cream background with a gold accent as the default; thin light-grey text on stone; vague words such as timeless and refined with no detail; a stock photo of an empty hotel room
Accessibility: Fine light type fails contrast (1.4.3), so use ink on stone at 7:1 for body and keep bronze for large text only. Keep tap targets 44px or more (2.5.8). Give each image meaningful alt text (1.1.1).
Performance: medium: large photographs carry the page; serve AVIF, set sizes and lazy-load below the fold.
Checklist: No more than three colours; photographs are the owner's own and high resolution; body text passes 7:1; contact details and prices policy are easy to find; spacing is consistent

Aliases: Documentary photography|Full-bleed photo story|Photo essay|Honest photography
Keywords: photography, documentary, full-bleed, captions, photo-essay, charity, farm, venue, honest, story
Looks Like: Full-bleed photographs of actual people and places, with short plain captions and little else on screen. Text is small, sits beside or below the image and says who, where and when.
Use When: photographer, charity, farm, venue, community group, campaign, church, local news
Avoid When: Businesses with no good photographs, and shops that need dense product listings. Weak images cannot carry the page.
Palette: Let the photograph set the colour; use a plain neutral frame. Starting colours: #FFFFFF page, #151515 ink, #5A5A5A caption text, #C23B22 one action colour.
Type Approach: A plain readable sans for captions and a sturdy serif for headings (Source Serif 4 with Public Sans). Captions at 15-16px, headlines at modest size so they do not fight the photograph.
Layout: Full-width images with captions below, then short text sections of 60 characters per line. Alternate wide and narrow images and keep one story per screen.
Motion: Images load with a 300ms fade and hold still; no parallax. Reduced motion shows images immediately.
Slop Habits: Stock photos of people at laptops; a hero image with a dark overlay and centred slogan; captions that say nothing such as Our team; a carousel of the same shot
Accessibility: Write alt text and captions that describe the scene and name the people (1.1.1). Captions over images need 4.5:1, so place them below. Carousels must pause (2.2.2); prefer a plain sequence. Set width and height to avoid layout shift.
Performance: high: many large images; use responsive srcset, AVIF or WebP and lazy-load all but the first.
Checklist: Every photograph is the owner's own and has permission from people shown; captions say who, where and when; alt text is written; images have width and height; layout holds at 375px
